title: Thin Lens Formula

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 12 — Ray Optics and Optical Instruments

explanation: The thin lens formula relates the object distance (u), image distance (v), and focal length (f) for a thin lens, using the Cartesian sign convention (distances measured from the optical center, with distances in the direction of incident light taken as positive). A converging (convex) lens has a positive focal length; a diverging (concave) lens has a negative focal length.
resultUnit: Same length unit used for u and f
conditions: Assumes a thin lens and paraxial rays (rays close to the principal axis); requires consistent sign convention throughout the calculation

workedExample.scenario: An object is placed 30 cm from a convex lens of focal length 10 cm (u = -30 cm using Cartesian convention).
workedExample.result: v = 15 cm (a real image forms 15 cm from the lens)

commonMistakes: Mixing sign conventions mid-calculation — the single most common source of errors in lens/mirror problems.
Forgetting that a diverging (concave) lens always has a negative focal length in the Cartesian convention.
genZNote: The lens formula only works if you commit to ONE sign convention for the entire problem — switching halfway through is where most marks get lost.
